passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the hearts of his officials, that I may perform these miraculous signs of Mine among them, and that you may tell your children and grandchildren how severely I dealt with the Egyptians when I performed miraculous signs among them, so that all of you may know that I am the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to go to Pharaoh.
The LORD said, “I have hardened Pharaoh’s heart.
I have also hardened the hearts of his officials.
I did this so I can show my miraculous signs among them.
You will tell your son and your grandson what I did in Egypt.
You will tell them how I punished the Egyptians.
You will tell them about the signs I did among them.
You will know that I am the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בֹּ֖א אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה כִּֽי־ אֲנִ֞י הִכְבַּ֤דְתִּי אֶת־ לִבּוֹ֙ וְאֶת־ לֵ֣ב עֲבָדָ֔יו לְמַ֗עַן שִׁתִ֛י אֹתֹתַ֥י אֵ֖לֶּה בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃ וּלְמַ֡עַן תְּסַפֵּר֩ בְּאָזְנֵ֨י בִנְךָ֜ וּבֶן־ בִּנְךָ֗ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִתְעַלַּ֙לְתִּי֙ בְּמִצְרַ֔יִם וְאֶת־ אֹתֹתַ֖י אֲשֶׁר־ שַׂ֣מְתִּי בָ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּי־ אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and told him, “This is what the LORD, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me? Let My people go, so that they may worship Me.
passages.sermon:
Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh.
They spoke to Pharaoh.
They said, “The LORD is the God of the Hebrews.
The LORD says this to you.
How long will you refuse to humble yourself before Me?
Let My people go.
They must worship Me.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאַהֲרֹן֮ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹה֒ וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָֽעִבְרִ֔ים עַד־ מָתַ֣י מֵאַ֔נְתָּ לֵעָנֹ֖ת מִפָּנָ֑י שַׁלַּ֥ח עַמִּ֖י וְיַֽעַבְדֻֽנִי׃

passages.text: But if you refuse to let My people go, I will bring locusts into your territory tomorrow.
passages.sermon: God spoke to Pharaoh through Moses.\r\nGod said, "If you refuse to let My people go, I will act."\r\nI will bring locusts into your land tomorrow.
passages.original: כִּ֛י אִם־ מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לְשַׁלֵּ֣חַ אֶת־ עַמִּ֑י הִנְנִ֨י מֵבִ֥יא מָחָ֛ר אַרְבֶּ֖ה בִּגְבֻלֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: They will cover the face of the land so that no one can see it. They will devour whatever is left after the hail and eat every tree that grows in your fields.
passages.sermon:
God sent Moses and Aaron to warn Pharaoh.
God is the God of the Hebrews.
God said locusts will come if Pharaoh refuses to let the Israelites go.
The locusts will cover the face of the land.
No one will be able to see the ground.
The locusts will eat everything left after the hail.
They will eat every tree that grows in the fields.
passages.original: וְכִסָּה֙ אֶת־ עֵ֣ין הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יוּכַ֖ל לִרְאֹ֣ת אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְאָכַ֣ל׀ אֶת־ יֶ֣תֶר הַפְּלֵטָ֗ה הַנִּשְׁאֶ֤רֶת לָכֶם֙ מִן־ הַבָּרָ֔ד וְאָכַל֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעֵ֔ץ הַצֹּמֵ֥חַ לָכֶ֖ם מִן־ הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: They will fill your houses and the houses of all your officials and every Egyptian—something neither your fathers nor your grandfathers have seen since the day they came into this land.’ ” Then Moses turned and left Pharaoh’s presence.
passages.sermon:
Locusts will fill your house.
Locusts will fill the houses of all your officials.
Locusts will fill the houses of every Egyptian.
No one has seen anything like this before.
Your fathers have not seen it.
Your grandfathers have not seen it.
This has not happened since the day they came into this land.
Moses turned away from Pharaoh.
Moses left Pharaoh’s presence.
passages.original: וּמָלְא֨וּ בָתֶּ֜יךָ וּבָתֵּ֣י כָל־ עֲבָדֶיךָ֮ וּבָתֵּ֣י כָל־ מִצְרַיִם֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ רָא֤וּ אֲבֹתֶ֙יךָ֙ וַאֲב֣וֹת אֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ מִיּ֗וֹם הֱיוֹתָם֙ עַל־ הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּ֥פֶן וַיֵּצֵ֖א מֵעִ֥ם פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Pharaoh’s officials asked him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the people go, so that they may worship the LORD their God. Do you not yet realize that Egypt is in ruins?”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Pharaoh had officials who served him.
The officials spoke to Pharaoh.
They asked Pharaoh a question.
They said, “How long will this man be a trap for us?”
They called Moses “this man.”
They told Pharaoh, “Let the people go.”
They meant the Israelites.
They said, “Let them worship the LORD their God.”
They asked Pharaoh, “Do you not yet know?”
They said, “Egypt is ruined.”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ עַבְדֵ֨י פַרְעֹ֜ה אֵלָ֗יו עַד־ מָתַי֙ יִהְיֶ֨ה זֶ֥ה לָ֙נוּ֙ לְמוֹקֵ֔שׁ שַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְיַֽעַבְד֖וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֑ם הֲטֶ֣רֶם תֵּדַ֔ע כִּ֥י אָבְדָ֖ה מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. “Go, worship the LORD your God,” he said. “But who exactly will be going?”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron back to him.
Moses and Aaron were leaders of the Israelites.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh said, “Go and worship the LORD your God.”
Pharaoh asked them a question.
Pharaoh said, “Who exactly will be going?”
passages.original: וַיּוּשַׁ֞ב אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֤ה וְאֶֽת־ אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם לְכ֥וּ עִבְד֖וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם מִ֥י וָמִ֖י הַהֹלְכִֽים׃

passages.text: “We will go with our young and old,” Moses replied. “We will go with our sons and daughters, and with our flocks and herds, for we must hold a feast to the LORD.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses led the Israelites.
Moses said, “We will go with our young people.
We will go with our old people.
We will go with our sons.
We will go with our daughters.
We will take our flocks.
We will take our herds.
We must go because we will hold a feast to the LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה בִּנְעָרֵ֥ינוּ וּבִזְקֵנֵ֖ינוּ נֵלֵ֑ךְ בְּבָנֵ֨ינוּ וּבִבְנוֹתֵ֜נוּ בְּצֹאנֵ֤נוּ וּבִבְקָרֵ֙נוּ֙ נֵלֵ֔ךְ כִּ֥י חַג־ יְהוָ֖ה לָֽנוּ׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh told them, “May the LORD be with you if I ever let you go with your little ones. Clearly you are bent on evil.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh said, “May the LORD be with you if I ever let you go with your little ones.”
Pharaoh did not trust Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh believed they planned something evil.
Pharaoh said, “Clearly you are bent on evil.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם יְהִ֨י כֵ֤ן יְהוָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר אֲשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶתְכֶ֖ם וְאֶֽת־ טַפְּכֶ֑ם רְא֕וּ כִּ֥י רָעָ֖ה נֶ֥גֶד פְּנֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: No, only the men may go and worship the LORD, since that is what you have been requesting.” And Moses and Aaron were driven from Pharaoh’s presence.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh said, “No, it will not be as you ask.”
Pharaoh said, “Only the men may go.”
Pharaoh said, “Go and worship the LORD.”
Pharaoh said, “This is what you have been requesting.”
Pharaoh drove Moses and Aaron away from his presence.
passages.original: לֹ֣א כֵ֗ן לְכֽוּ־ נָ֤א הַגְּבָרִים֙ וְעִבְד֣וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אֹתָ֖הּ אַתֶּ֣ם מְבַקְשִׁ֑ים וַיְגָ֣רֶשׁ אֹתָ֔ם מֵאֵ֖ת פְּנֵ֥י פַרְעֹֽה׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt, so that the locusts may swarm over it and devour every plant in the land—everything that the hail has left behind.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to act.
The LORD said, "Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt."
The LORD said locusts would come over the land of Egypt.
The LORD said the locusts would eat every plant in the land.
The LORD said the locusts would eat everything the hail had left behind.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֨ה יָדְךָ֜ עַל־ אֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בָּֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְיַ֖עַל עַל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְיֹאכַל֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִשְׁאִ֖יר הַבָּרָֽד׃

passages.text: So Moses stretched out his staff over the land of Egypt, and throughout that day and night the LORD sent an east wind across the land. By morning the east wind had brought the locusts.
passages.sermon:
Moses was God's chosen leader.
Moses held his staff over the land of Egypt.
The LORD acted with power.
The LORD sent an east wind over Egypt.
The wind blew all that day.
The wind blew all that night.
Morning came.
The east wind brought locusts into Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨ט מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶת־ מַטֵּהוּ֮ עַל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַיִם֒ וַֽיהוָ֗ה נִהַ֤ג ר֥וּחַ קָדִים֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ כָּל־ הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וְכָל־ הַלָּ֑יְלָה הַבֹּ֣קֶר הָיָ֔ה וְר֙וּחַ֙ הַקָּדִ֔ים נָשָׂ֖א אֶת־ הָאַרְבֶּֽה׃

passages.text: The locusts swarmed across the land and settled over the entire territory of Egypt. Never before had there been so many locusts, and never again will there be.
passages.sermon:
Locusts swarmed over the whole land of Egypt.
They settled in every part of Egypt.
There were more locusts than ever before.
There will never be so many locusts again.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַל הָֽאַרְבֶּ֗ה עַ֚ל כָּל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיָּ֕נַח בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל מִצְרָ֑יִם כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד לְ֠פָנָיו לֹא־ הָ֨יָה כֵ֤ן אַרְבֶּה֙ כָּמֹ֔הוּ וְאַחֲרָ֖יו לֹ֥א יִֽהְיֶה־ כֵּֽן׃

passages.text: They covered the face of all the land until it was black, and they consumed all the plants on the ground and all the fruit on the trees that the hail had left behind. Nothing green was left on any tree or plant in all the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The locusts covered the face of all the land of Egypt.
They made the land dark.
The locusts ate every plant on the ground.
They ate all the fruit on the trees.
The hail had left some fruit on the trees.
The locusts ate what the hail had left.
No green thing remained on any tree.
No green plant remained in the fields.
This happened everywhere in the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיְכַ֞ס אֶת־ עֵ֣ין כָּל־ הָאָרֶץ֮ וַתֶּחְשַׁ֣ךְ הָאָרֶץ֒ וַיֹּ֜אכַל אֶת־ כָּל־ עֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָ֗רֶץ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ פְּרִ֣י הָעֵ֔ץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹתִ֖יר הַבָּרָ֑ד וְלֹא־ נוֹתַ֨ר כָּל־ יֶ֧רֶק בָּעֵ֛ץ וּבְעֵ֥שֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Pharaoh quickly summoned Moses and Aaron and said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Pharaoh saw the land covered by locusts.
Pharaoh acted quickly.
Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh said, “I have sinned.”
Pharaoh said, “I have sinned against the LORD your God.”
Pharaoh said, “I have sinned against you.”
passages.original: וַיְמַהֵ֣ר פַּרְעֹ֔ה לִקְרֹ֖א לְמֹשֶׁ֣ה וּֽלְאַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר חָטָ֛אתִי לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֖ם וְלָכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Now please forgive my sin once more and appeal to the LORD your God, that He may remove this death from me.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses and Aaron.
Pharaoh said, “Please forgive my sin this time.
Pray to the LORD your God for me.
Ask Him to take away this death from me.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה שָׂ֣א נָ֤א חַטָּאתִי֙ אַ֣ךְ הַפַּ֔עַם וְהַעְתִּ֖ירוּ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם וְיָסֵר֙ מֵֽעָלַ֔י רַ֖ק אֶת־ הַמָּ֥וֶת הַזֶּֽה׃

passages.text: So Moses left Pharaoh’s presence and appealed to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of the Israelites.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Moses left Pharaoh.
Moses prayed to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֖א מֵעִ֣ם פַּרְעֹ֑ה וַיֶּעְתַּ֖ר אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And the LORD changed the wind to a very strong west wind that carried off the locusts and blew them into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained anywhere in Egypt.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD acted with great power.
The LORD changed the wind.
The LORD made the wind blow very strongly from the west.
The LORD used the wind to carry away the locusts.
The LORD blew the locusts into the Red Sea.
No locusts remained in Egypt.
Egypt was completely free of locusts.
passages.original: וַיַּהֲפֹ֨ךְ יְהוָ֤ה רֽוּחַ־ יָם֙ חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֔ד וַיִּשָּׂא֙ אֶת־ הָ֣אַרְבֶּ֔ה וַיִּתְקָעֵ֖הוּ יָ֣מָּה סּ֑וּף לֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר֙ אַרְבֶּ֣ה אֶחָ֔ד בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he would not let the Israelites go.
passages.sermon: The LORD acted with power.\r\nThe LORD made Pharaoh’s heart stubborn.\r\nPharaoh refused to let the Israelites go.
passages.original: וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְלֹ֥א שִׁלַּ֖ח אֶת־ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, so that darkness may spread over the land of Egypt—a palpable darkness.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to act.
The LORD said, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven.”
The LORD wanted darkness to cover the land of Egypt.
The LORD said the darkness would be felt.
The LORD described the darkness as palpable.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה נְטֵ֤ה יָֽדְךָ֙ עַל־ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וִ֥יהִי חֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְיָמֵ֖שׁ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃

passages.text: So Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven, and total darkness covered all the land of Egypt for three days.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
God commanded Moses to act.
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven.
Darkness came over all the land of Egypt.
The darkness was total.
This darkness lasted for three days.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥ט מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־ יָד֖וֹ עַל־ הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיְהִ֧י חֹֽשֶׁךְ־ אֲפֵלָ֛ה בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: No one could see anyone else, and for three days no one left his place. Yet all the Israelites had light in their dwellings.
passages.sermon:
God sent darkness over Egypt.
The darkness lasted three days.
No Egyptian could see another person.
No Egyptian left his place for three days.
All the Israelites had light in their homes.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ רָא֞וּ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ אָחִ֗יו וְלֹא־ קָ֛מוּ אִ֥ישׁ מִתַּחְתָּ֖יו שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֑ים וּֽלְכָל־ בְּנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל הָ֥יָה א֖וֹר בְּמוֹשְׁבֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh summoned Moses and said, “Go, worship the LORD. Even your little ones may go with you; only your flocks and herds must stay behind.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh called Moses.
Pharaoh spoke to Moses.
Pharaoh said, “Go and worship the LORD.”
Pharaoh said, “Your children may go with you.”
Pharaoh said, “Your flocks and herds must stay here.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לְכוּ֙ עִבְד֣וּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה רַ֛ק צֹאנְכֶ֥ם וּבְקַרְכֶ֖ם יֻצָּ֑ג גַּֽם־ טַפְּכֶ֖ם יֵלֵ֥ךְ עִמָּכֶֽם׃

passages.text: But Moses replied, “You must also provide us with sacrifices and burnt offerings to present to the LORD our God.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses said, “You must give us sacrifices.
You must also give us burnt offerings.
We will offer them to the LORD our God.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֔ה גַּם־ אַתָּ֛ה תִּתֵּ֥ן בְּיָדֵ֖נוּ זְבָחִ֣ים וְעֹל֑וֹת וְעָשִׂ֖ינוּ לַיהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Even our livestock must go with us; not a hoof will be left behind, for we will need some of them to worship the LORD our God, and we will not know how we are to worship the LORD until we arrive.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to Pharaoh.
Moses said that all our livestock must go with us.
We will not leave even one hoof behind.
We will take animals from our livestock.
We need them to worship the LORD our God.
We do not know what we must offer to the LORD.
We will only know what to do when we arrive.
passages.original: וְגַם־ מִקְנֵ֜נוּ יֵלֵ֣ךְ עִמָּ֗נוּ לֹ֤א תִשָּׁאֵר֙ פַּרְסָ֔ה כִּ֚י מִמֶּ֣נּוּ נִקַּ֔ח לַעֲבֹ֖ד אֶת־ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וַאֲנַ֣חְנוּ לֹֽא־ נֵדַ֗ע מַֽה־ נַּעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־ יְהוָ֔ה עַד־ בֹּאֵ֖נוּ שָֽׁמָּה׃

passages.text: But the LORD hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he was unwilling to let them go.
passages.sermon: The LORD acted.\r\nThe LORD made Pharaoh’s heart hard.\r\nPharaoh refused to let the Israelites go.
passages.original: וַיְחַזֵּ֥ק יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֑ה וְלֹ֥א אָבָ֖ה לְשַׁלְּחָֽם׃

passages.text: “Depart from me!” Pharaoh said to Moses. “Make sure you never see my face again, for on the day you see my face, you will die.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
\r\nMoses was the leader of the Israelites.
\r\nPharaoh spoke to Moses.
\r\nPharaoh said, “Leave me.”
\r\nPharaoh warned Moses.
\r\nPharaoh said, “Do not come to see me again.”
\r\nPharaoh said, “If you see my face again, you will die that day.”
passages.original: וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ ל֥וֹ פַרְעֹ֖ה לֵ֣ךְ מֵעָלָ֑י הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֗ אֶל־ תֹּ֙סֶף֙ רְא֣וֹת פָּנַ֔י כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם רְאֹתְךָ֥ פָנַ֖י תָּמֽוּת׃

passages.text: “As you say,” Moses replied, “I will never see your face again.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of the Israelites.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh told Moses not to come before him again.
Moses answered Pharaoh.
Moses said, “You have spoken correctly.”
Moses said, “I will not see your face again.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֖ה כֵּ֣ן דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ לֹא־ אֹסִ֥ף ע֖וֹד רְא֥וֹת פָּנֶֽיךָ׃פ
